History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old man with 3 days of profuse watery diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, mild vomiting, and subjective fever—likely acute gastroenteritis; advised oral rehydration, symptomatic care, and 48-hour review.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Profuse watery diarrhoea.
• Onset/duration: Began 3 days ago (Monday/Tuesday).  
• Frequency/severity: ~hourly bowel motions while awake; described as “fluids coming out.”  
• Character/progression: Unchanged/not improving.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Crampy mid-lower abdominal pain, intermittent, ~6/10.  
  – Nausea; occasional vomiting (worse after milk).  
  – Subjective fever (“burning up,” no temperature recorded).  
  – Slightly reduced urine frequency but still voiding.  
• Denies: Blood in stool.  
• Exposures: Brother has had similar illness for 5 days and is “getting better.” No clear food or travel trigger identified.  
• Diet/fluids: Taking water, coffee, able to eat small meals but stools remain loose.  
• ROS (pertinent negatives): No focal abdominal tenderness reported, no rectal bleeding, no chest pain, no urinary burning.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
• Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented (used for pain/fever).
• No regular prescription medications.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with mother and sister; brother lives separately.  
• Employment: Office job in government (Central London).  
• Smoking: Occasional social smoker (mainly on Fridays).  
• Alcohol: Beer on some weekdays; binge drinking once or twice a month.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  
• Diet: Often purchases takeaway food; seldom eats with family.  
• Financial/lifestyle issues: Concern about taking time off work; otherwise not detailed.

Family History:
• Father: Stage III colon cancer (current).  
• No other gastrointestinal or major illnesses noted in family.

Physical Examination:
• Conducted via telehealth; no vitals or direct examination performed.

Investigations:
• None performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk.
  – Encourage oral rehydration with oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) and clear fluids.  
  – Soft diet (soups, mashed foods) as tolerated; avoid dairy if worsens symptoms.  
  – Continue Paracetamol for fever/pain.  
  – Avoid alcohol until recovery.  
  – Monitor urine output; aim for regular passing of pale urine.  
  – Safety-net: Seek medical review if no improvement within 48 hours, worsening symptoms, inability to keep fluids down, signs of dehydration (dizziness, reduced urine, dry mouth), or blood in stool.

General Plan items:
  – Educate regarding hand hygiene to prevent spread within household.  
  – Consider stool cultures and blood tests if symptoms persist beyond expected course or red-flag features develop.  
  – Follow-up: Telephone review in 48 hours if not improving; earlier if concerns arise.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: No documented vitals, weight, or physical exam findings; no medication doses; no allergy verification beyond NKA; no lab or stool investigations.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional minor audio gaps but clinically adequate.
